title: Prefill: sparse MLA + prologue
shape: DEP16 F16K (3 x 5,461 tok) at L78K, NVFP4, 96 heads/GPU, top-2048, FP8 KV 576 B rows; 24 DSA layers
basis: MEASURED standalone per layer at F16K x 24 (runs/P-MLA/run1,run5,run8: trtllm-gen 2.08 ms + quant 0.204 + pad 0.175 + insert 0.042 + gate 0.129 = 2.63 ms/layer = 63 ms/step; in-step F8K x2 = 67); model ach 15.9 (optables nvfp4_modelopt|P3-16|prefill); measured gather floor implies ~26 ms/step (model omits the per-token gather)
gap_analysis: Per F16K layer (1 GPU, run1): trtllm-gen sparse MLA 2129.5 us (3.29 PF on the 96 real heads; model 643), quant 204.1 + head pad 173.4 + KV insert 42.0 (model prologue 10.9), gate_mul 128.8 (model 7.7). Hardware probes (run2/run3): tcgen05 FP8 2x-K MMA reaches the full rate only with A in TMEM; every SMEM operand byte costs 1/128 clk (128 B/clk/SM operand fetch, measured flat across N and majorness), so both-operands-in-SMEM forms (keys-on-M / transposed) cap at 43% (N=96). TMA writes into SMEM at about 55 B/clk do not slow a full-rate TS MMA (no read/write contention measured). TMA tile::gather4 is issue-bound at about 56 clk per instruction per issuing warp: 1/2/4 warps reach 4.1/7.0/10.9 TB/s of 576 B row gathers; plain LDG gathers reach 18.2 TB/s (1064 us per F16K layer). The per-token gather (2048 rows x 576 B = 19.3 GB per F16K layer, L2->SM) is not in the model (kv_B counts 135 MB of unique KV), and neither is the SMEM operand traffic (36.5 GB per layer at 128 B/clk/SM = 565 us). The stock kernel's 2-CTA HVPerCta256 layout most likely re-gathers V (about 1.9x the minimum gather bytes; inferred from its name and FlashMLA's documented equivalent, ncu is not in the image), which at the measured gather rates explains its 2.1 ms. Measured gather floor (run4): ~18 TB/s for random 576 B rows -> sparse_mla cannot go below ~1.07 ms/layer (25.7 ms/step at F16K) with one gather per token-row; the model (643 us/layer) misses this term. Proposed corrected achievable for the family: 24 x (1.07 + 0.019) = ~26 ms/step (model fix pending owner review).
inefficiencies: Stock trtllm-gen kernel: 2-CTA M128 (heads padded 96->128), V re-gathered per CTA half -> about 1.9x the minimum L2->SM bytes; gather-bound (HYPOTHESIS from name + timing; ncu unavailable)

Perf model omits the per-token KV row gather (19.3 GB/layer at F16K) and the SMEM operand traffic: true floor is max(MMA 566 us at 128 padded rows, SMEM reads 565 us, gather 19.3 GB / L2 rate) per layer
Query quant and head pad are two separate full passes because the in-place RoPE concat disables the fused quant_pad kernel (MEASURED 377 us/layer at F16K; fix implemented on the branch, measuring)
gate_mul is a separate pass over [T, 12288] BF16 (MEASURED 129 us/layer)
FlashInfer prims_ts sparse MLA refuses sm_107 in this image: no drop-in alternative
rubin_features: tcgen05 FP8 kind::f8f6f4 with the Rubin 2x-K instruction descriptor
TMEM A operands (Q, P) to stay under the SMEM operand-fetch limit
576-column exclusive TMEM allocation (2-CTA M128 folded O 256 + S + full Q in TMEM)
cta_group::2 M128 MMA pairs with TMA tile::gather4 multicast to the pair (gather each row once)
many-warp TMA gather issue (gather4 is issue-bound per warp)
oversized (>227 KiB) shared memory carveout for deeper KV rings
PDL between prologue, attention and w_uv
plan: 1. DONE measure stock chain per kernel at F8K/F16K; probe MMA operand-fetch, SMEM write contention, TMEM copy, gather4 issue rate
2. Land the prologue fix: one fused concat+FP8 quant+head pad kernel (bitwise vs stock) instead of quant + pad passes (branch wired; measure in bench and step)
3. Gather floor with 8/16 issuing warps (run4) -> record the model fix (gather + SMEM terms) with measured numbers

4. New prefill sparse-MLA kernel (specialized_prefill): 2-CTA M128 TS (Q fully in TMEM via exclusive 576 cols), gather each row once with gather4 multicast to the pair from 8+ issuing warps, P in TMEM, O folded 256 cols, persistent over tokens; target the gather/SMEM floor
5. gate_mul fused into a w_uv batched GEMM epilogue (stock rounding: bf16(out) * bf16(sigmoid))
6. Unit tests vs stock, microbench F8K/F16K, step A/B on the INFRA harness, landed-ready
